items.stem: When you read English, which way do your eyes move along a line of words?

options.rationale: Correct: English is read from left to right.
That is the direction for some other languages, not English.
We move down the page, not up it.
Lines of text are read straight across, not in circles.

items.explanation: Correct: English is read from left to right.

items.stem: You come to a word you do not know. What is the best first thing to try?

options.text: Sound out the letters and blend them
options.rationale: Correct: decoding the sounds is the best first strategy.

options.text: Skip the word and never look back
options.rationale: Skipping it loses the meaning of the sentence.

options.text: Say any word that starts the same
options.rationale: Guessing from the first letter often gives the wrong word.
Giving up does not help you read the word.

items.explanation: Correct: decoding the sounds is the best first strategy.

items.stem: Which TWO things help you understand a story while you read? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: pictures give clues to meaning.

options.text: Thinking about what has happened so far
options.rationale: Correct: holding the story in mind aids understanding.

options.text: Reading as fast as possible with no thinking
options.rationale: Speed without understanding does not build meaning.

options.text: Covering the words with your hand
options.rationale: You cannot read the words if they are covered.

items.explanation: Correct: pictures give clues to meaning.
